name: Sequencing a Home Remodel and ADU Addition Together in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County sequence design and construction when the project includes both a major home remodel and a new ADU?
mainEntity.text: How do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County sequence design and construction when the project includes both a major home remodel and a new ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: Combining a significant home remodel with an ADU addition in Los Angeles County can be efficient but requires careful sequencing. A seasoned ADU additions contractor will usually coordinate a unified design process so the remodel and ADU share consistent structural, utility, and aesthetic decisions. However, they may separate scopes in the plans and permits for clarity and to keep inspections manageable. Structurally, they often tackle foundation, framing, and major utility upgrades first, especially those that serve both the main house and the new ADU. This might include upsizing the electrical panel, reworking the main sewer line, or modifying load‑bearing walls. Once core systems are in place, they phase interior work so some areas of the home stay functional while others are under construction, which is critical if you plan to live on site. Finishes for the remodel and ADU may be staggered to spread costs and balance labor. Ask contractors how they have phased similar combined projects, whether they recommend one master permit or multiple permits, and how they would protect areas of the home that are already remodeled from damage during ADU construction. A clear, written phasing plan helps manage disruption and keeps the overall project more predictable.
acceptedAnswer.description: When a project combines a major remodel and an ADU addition, contractors often phase design together but separate scopes in permits and budgets. They typically prioritize structural and utility work that serves both, then sequence finish work to minimize rework and allow parts of the home to remain livable.
